tools.name: run_python
tools.title: Run Python on inline data
tools.description: Run Python code on the data given with this call and get back what it printed and the files it wrote. Each data entry is a file in the current folder, under its name, read-only. Write every result file directly into the out/ folder: tables as CSV, for example df.to_csv('out/counts.csv', index=False), and charts as PNG, for example plt.savefig('out/chart.png', dpi=100). Only .png, .csv, .txt, .md and .json files come back, at most 8: an image up to 512 KiB, a text up to 256 KiB, 1 MiB in all. files lists every file written, with returned false and a hint for one that did not come back; nothing is kept after the call. Installed: pandas, numpy, scipy, matplotlib. There is no network and nothing can be installed. Use threads, not multiprocessing. The code runs as a script with a time limit; an error or timeout is in stderr. stdout and stderr are cut in the middle when long (truncated is then true), so print summaries, not whole tables. Cite job_id as the source of figures the code computed.

InlineData.description:
One data entry: a text the call brings, written as a read-only file of the job's folder.

Attributes:
    name: The file's name.
    content: Its text, written as UTF-8.

name.description: The file's name in the current folder, such as passages.json: ending .json, .csv, .txt or .md.
name.title: Name

InlineData.title: InlineData

inputSchema.description:
Arguments of inline ``run_python``, validated with the caller's wall cap as ``context={"wall_cap": ...}``.

Attributes:
    code: The Python to run, as a script.
    data: The data, each entry a file of the current folder.
    time_limit_s: Seconds the job may run, or ``None`` for the caller's cap.

code.description: The Python code to run, as a script; at most 50000 characters. Print what you need to see, and write every result file directly into out/.
code.title: Code

data.description: The data, at most 8 entries and 512 KiB in all: each is a read-only file of the current folder.
data.title: Data

time_limit_s.description: Seconds the code may run, from 5 to the most this service allows; leave it out for that most. The code gets 9/10 of it, so that stderr can say it timed out.

inputSchema.title: InlinePythonRequest

OutputInfo.description:
One file the code wrote into ``out/``, and whether it came back.

Attributes:
    name: Its name, as the code wrote it.
    mime: Its media type.
    bytes: Its size in bytes.
    returned: Whether it came back with this answer.

name.description: Its name in out/, as the code wrote it.
name.title: Name

returned.description: True if it came back with this answer; the hint says why one did not.
returned.title: Returned

OutputInfo.title: OutputInfo

outputSchema.description:
What inline ``run_python`` answers; sent with its ``None`` fields.

Attributes:
    stdout: What the code printed.
    stderr: Its warnings and errors.
    truncated: Whether stdout or stderr was cut in the middle.
    job_id: The id of the run.
    files: Every file the code wrote: those that came back, then those that did not.
    hint: What to tell the user, or how to go on.
    reason: Always ``None`` on a result; an error result names its reason there.

stderr.description: Its warnings and errors; a traceback ends with the error.
stderr.title: Stderr

truncated.description: True if stdout or stderr was cut in the middle to fit the result limit.
truncated.title: Truncated

job_id.description: The id of this run; cite it as the source of what the code computed.
job_id.title: Job Id

files.description: Every file written into out/: those that came back first.
files.title: Files

hint.description: What to tell the user, or how to go on.
hint.title: Hint

reason.description: None on a result; an error result names its reason here.
reason.title: Reason

outputSchema.title: InlinePythonResult
